claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies with conventional internal boundaries.
A minor Nb addition during processing and heat treatment will segregate to internal lamellar or colony boundaries.
Boundary segregation of Nb will enhance interfacial cohesion.
Enhanced interfacial cohesion will delay microcrack initiation.
Enhanced interfacial cohesion will delay microcrack propagation.
Microalloying-induced interface tuning will refine the lamellar structure or lamellar spacing.
Lamellar refinement will improve strain-hardening characteristics.
Improved strain hardening and delayed microcracking will increase tensile strength.
Improved strain hardening and delayed microcracking will increase room-temperature tensile ductility.
The microalloyed alloy will exhibit a statistically significant increase in tensile strength relative to the unmodified baseline.
The microalloyed alloy will exhibit a statistically significant increase in elongation to failure at room temperature relative to the unmodified baseline.
The conventional baseline has limited strength and room-temperature ductility because microcracks initiate along internal boundaries.
Excessive microalloying addition may cause detrimental precipitate formation.
Non-optimal heat treatment may cause coarsening.
Precipitate formation or coarsening may negate the proposed improvements in strength and ductility.
